requirements.requirement: Establish/confirm the real private routed path node2 <-> node1 <-> node3 (addressing and routes) needed to apply directional shaping
requirements.summary: Executor discovered node1 eth1/eth2 and node2/node3 enp8s0 as the unaddressed private links (distinct from shared mgmt network), assigned 10.50.1.0/24 and 10.50.2.0/24, added static routes via nmcli on node2/node3 and VyOS config on node1, and verified end-to-end connectivity (ping and iperf3 both directions) both before and after all three nodes were rebooted.

requirements.requirement: Limit traffic from node2 toward node3 to 1 Mbit/s
requirements.summary: An HTB qdisc with u32 filter matching dst 10.50.2.0/24 was applied on node2's enp8s0 (the node3-facing interface), classifying that traffic into a 1mbit-capped class. Baseline unshaped throughput was ~18.7 Gbit/s; after shaping, UDP iperf3 node2->node3 measured sender 1.05 Mbit/s / receiver 973 Kbit/s, directly at the 1 Mbit/s target. Shaping was persisted via a systemd unit and re-verified functioning after a full node2 reboot, with post-reboot throughput ~1.13/0.96 Mbit/s.

requirements.requirement: Leave traffic from node3 toward node2 unrestricted
requirements.summary: No shaping was applied on node3, and the node2 HTB filter only matches traffic destined for 10.50.2.0/24, leaving the default class (1:30, 10gbit) for other traffic including the return path. iperf3 measured node3->node2 throughput at ~1.07 Gbit/s immediately after shaping was applied and ~1.21 Gbit/s after node3 was rebooted, confirming the reverse direction remained unrestricted both before and after shaping/restart.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct measurement evidence: the private node2<->node1<->node3 path was correctly identified and addressed, node2->node3 traffic was capped to ~1 Mbit/s via a node2-side HTB/u32 tc configuration (persisted via systemd and reverified after a reboot), and node3->node2 traffic remained unrestricted (~1-19 Gbit/s) both before and after restarts. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed on all three nodes with clear pre-restart boot identity, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered network/shaping state, cross-checked successfully against the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshots. The main deduction is operational hygiene: iperf3 test tooling and firewalld port openings used for verification were not cleaned up afterward, leaving minor unnecessary residue and an open (unused) port on node2 and node3.
limitations: TCP throughput test immediately after applying shaping (cmd-e953e5b375e848cf) showed throughput dropping to 0 mid-test; this appears to be an artifact of TCP behavior over a severely constrained link with sfq, not a failure of the cap itself, but it was not further explained.

Restart evidence, while thorough, is independent of the public task contract (no reboot/persistence requirement was stated); it is treated here as supplemental confidence-building evidence, not as a scored task requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: Core actions (topology discovery, IP/route configuration, tc HTB shaping, systemd persistence unit) were purposeful and directly tied to the task or to bounded verification. However, several testing-support mutations were left in place rather than cleaned up: firewalld ports 5201/tcp and 5201/udp were opened on node2 (cmd-2ef31826e77a4b90, cmd-f764bff3d8914c81) and node3 (cmd-1d30929542924bad, cmd-16792a45dc344382, cmd-dccfda45052e4260) for iperf3 testing and were never closed, leaving an unnecessary open port on both hosts after the iperf3 server processes were killed (cmd-c233c87718924a2e, cmd-1acdca96dfac4fae). Iperf3 packages (cmd-b9598b8f10d34b48, cmd-85cc0d12b95745ce) and associated log/pid files under /tmp also remained as residue on node2/node3 per the after_executor snapshot. These are low-risk, bounded artifacts (no failed services, no package-manager corruption, no unrelated config drift), but the unclosed firewall ports represent a minor weakened security posture that was not reverted.
